D020-D013_h001.question: I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I don’t know. Work’s always been high pressure, but lately, it’s like my mind won’t shut up. I’m on edge during shifts, second-guessing clearances, my hands sweat even when it’s not busy. I keep thinking something’s going to go wrong, even when everything’s under control. It’s not just the job, though. I wake up tense, like I’m already behind, and it’s hard to get out of bed. Some days I just sit there, staring at the ceiling. I used to run every morning—kept me sane—but now I can’t find the energy. I don’t feel like seeing friends, even my sister, who lives nearby. We were close, but I’ve been dodging her calls. I tell myself I should care more, but it’s like I’m watching my life from the outside. I can’t say there’s one thing that made this start—nothing big, anyway. No breakup, no loss. Just… slowly feeling like I’m sinking while still showing up, still doing the job. I don’t know if this is stress, sadness, or just burnout. I just know I don’t feel like myself.
D020-D013_h001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D020-D013_h001.answer: B & C. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe four or five? It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started. Work’s been busy, like it always is—managing teams, deadlines, server migrations—but I don’t know if that’s really it. I just feel… heavy. Not like I can’t get out of bed or anything, but I don’t enjoy things the way I used to. I cancelled drinks with friends a few times, not because I was overwhelmed, just because I didn’t feel like talking.  

I’ve been skipping the gym, even though I used to go religiously. My appetite’s down a little—nothing extreme—but I’ve lost a few pounds without trying. Sleep’s spotty. Some nights I’m out fast, others I’m up at 3 a.m. staring at the ceiling, thinking about nothing in particular.  

There hasn’t been one big thing that kicked this off—a breakup, a layoff, nothing like that. Just this constant low hum of exhaustion, like my system’s running on minimal power. I can still do my job, but it takes more effort. I don’t cry or feel hopeless, but I can’t remember the last time I genuinely laughed.  

I thought it’d pass, but here we are.
D020-D013_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D020-D013_h002.answer: B & C. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h003.question:
I’ve just been feeling really down lately—more than I ever have before. Some days, I’ll be playing in rehearsal and suddenly feel this wave of sadness come over me, and I have to fight not to cry. It’s embarrassing, especially with everyone focused and in tune. I used to find such joy in the music, but now it feels like I’m just going through the motions. I don’t practice as much at home. I’ll get home after work and just sit on the couch, too tired or heavy to pick up my violin.  

I’m not sleeping well—either I can’t fall asleep or I wake up too early and can’t get back to sleep. My appetite’s off, too. I’ve lost a little weight, though I’m not trying to. I don’t feel like hanging out with friends, even people I’ve known for years. I just don’t want to talk.  

I can’t pinpoint exactly when it started, maybe a few months ago. There was some tension at work last season—new conductor, more pressure—but honestly, it might’ve begun before that. I’m not even sure what’s wrong, or if it’s really “clinically” anything. I just feel… stuck.
D020-D013_h003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D020-D013_h003.answer: B & C. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h004.question: I’ve been feeling off for a while now—months, maybe. I can’t quite pinpoint when it started, but it’s like a fog that never lifts. I wake up tired, even after sleeping, and the day just feels heavy. I don’t cry often, but sometimes, sitting alone in my office after everyone’s left, I get this lump in my throat—just sadness without a clear reason. I’m divorced, so evenings are quiet, maybe too quiet. I used to enjoy reading case law, fine-tuning arguments, but now I lose focus. It’s not that I don’t care anymore—it’s like the energy’s been drained. I’m irritable, too. Small things at work set me off—missed deadlines from junior associates, even a misplaced file—stuff I used to brush off. I’ve lost a bit of weight, not on purpose. Appetite’s down. I don’t feel worthless, but I do wonder if I’m still any good at what I do. Some days are okay. On those, I almost believe I’m just going through a rough patch. I don’t know if this is from work stress, being alone, or just… aging. I can’t say anything major happened—no big case loss, no health scare—nothing that should knock me this off balance.
D020-D013_h004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D020-D013_h004.answer: B & C. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—hard to say exactly when it started. Since my husband passed, everything’s just felt heavier. I work in the kitchen at a care home, washing dishes and keeping things clean. It’s not much, but it’s work I can do. Only now, I don’t seem to have the energy like I used to. Some days, just standing there at the sink, my arms feel like lead, and my mind races—worried I’ll slip up, forget something, or get let go. I don’t sleep well either. I wake up around three or four, heart pounding, thinking about bills or how quiet the flat is.

I don’t cry all the time, but there’s this constant ache, like a dull sadness that never lifts. I don’t enjoy my tea like I used to, or the walk to work—even the radio doesn’t help. But I can’t say it’s every single day, or that I can’t get out of bed. I keep going. I just feel… rattled. Nervous and low, like I'm stuck between two places. I don’t know if it’s grief, stress, or something more—but it doesn’t feel temporary.
D020-D013_h005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D020-D013_h005.answer: B & C. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h006.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I’m not even sure anymore. Some days it’s like this heavy cloud just follows me, even in the middle of teaching class. I love my clients, but lately I’ve had to force myself to smile, to sound upbeat. I’ll be standing there cueing breath and movement, and suddenly my chest tightens—like I can’t catch my air. It doesn’t happen every day, but often enough that I notice. 

Sleep’s been spotty. I’ll wake up at 3 a.m. thinking about everything—my divorce, my mom’s health, whether I’m doing enough with my business. I don’t cry much, but I feel… numb. Drained. Appetite’s down a bit; I forget to eat until I’m dizzy. I used to meal prep religiously—now I’m lucky if I throw together a salad.

I wouldn’t say I’m hopeless, but I’m definitely not myself. I wonder if it’s just adjusting to being single again, or if it’s more than that. I function, but barely. It’s like I’m running on fumes, and I don’t know how much longer I can keep this up.
D020-D013_h006.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h006.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h007.question:
I’ve just been feeling so down lately, and I know it’s been hard since moving into this place—leaving my home after 50 years wasn’t easy. I miss my kitchen, my garden, even the noisy neighbors. Now, everything feels so quiet and… small. I don’t sleep well. I wake up early and can’t get back to sleep, just staring at the ceiling. Some days I don’t even want to get dressed.  

I used to enjoy the activities here—arts and crafts, the sing-alongs—but now I just sit in my chair most days. I’m not really angry, but I snap sometimes when the aides try to help me. I didn’t used to be that way. I’ll say things like “Leave me be,” even though deep down I know they’re just trying. My daughter comes when she can, but I hate seeing the look in her eyes—like she’s worried I’m giving up.  

I don’t feel like *myself*. I cry over little things—old photos, a familiar song on the radio. But I wouldn’t say I’m “depressed,” exactly. Just… worn out. Like my heart can’t catch up. It’s been months like this—some better days, more bad ones. I can’t tell if it’s grief or something more.
D020-D013_h007.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h007.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h008.question: I’ve just been feeling off for a few months now—can’t really put my finger on when it started, but it’s gotten harder to shake. I’m not sleeping great, either waking up way too early or not wanting to get out of bed at all. My focus at work’s been slipping; I’m making mistakes I wouldn’t have before, like misreading circuits or forgetting simple tasks. My boss hasn’t said anything yet, but I can tell he’s noticed. I used to hang out with the guys after shifts, grab a burger or play video games, but now I just go home and sit there. Don’t feel like talking, don’t feel like doing much of anything. I’m not sure if it’s because of everything happening lately—trying to prove myself on the job, money stuff, just… life—or if I’m just falling behind for no reason. I don’t feel sad exactly, but there’s this flatness, like I’m going through motions. No real hope, no real anger—just empty. I haven’t had thoughts about hurting myself or anything like that, but I do wonder if I’d care that much if things stayed this way. It’s not bad enough to call in sick, but it’s not *okay* either.
D020-D013_h008.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h008.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h009.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I don’t know. Things at home have been tense since my mother moved in after her stroke. It’s not that I don’t want to help, but everything feels heavier lately. I used to take pride in my work—designing spaces, picking the right fabrics, making clients’ houses feel like homes—but now I’ll start a project and just… stop. I leave emails unanswered, miss calls, cancel meetings last minute. It’s not like me.  

I’ve also been driving differently. I used to be careful, but last week I ran a red light without realizing. Not on purpose—my mind was somewhere else. And sometimes, when I’m upset, I’ll take the car and just drive, not really knowing where I’m going. I haven’t damaged anything or gotten in trouble, but it’s not safe. I know that.  

I’ve been short-tempered too. Snapping at my husband over little things—how he leaves his shoes out, the way he loads the dishwasher. Petty stuff. Then I feel guilty after. I don’t enjoy much these days—reading, gardening, even decorating. But I can’t say I feel *empty* all the time either. Some days are okay. Most aren’t. I’m not sure if this is just stress or something more. It’s affecting things I care about, though—my work, my marriage. That’s why I’m here.
D020-D013_h009.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h009.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I’ve lost track. Most days I wake up without any energy, like I’m dragging myself through concrete. I don’t cry all the time, but there are moments—usually late at night—when I just feel completely empty, and I’ll break down without really knowing why. It’s been hard to explain to my wife. I love her, I do, but I’ve been distant, not interested in things we used to enjoy together.

Work’s been especially rough. As an air traffic controller, you have to be sharp, every second. Lately, I’ve had trouble concentrating during shifts. Not in a dangerous way, but I notice it—my mind wanders, I second-guess clearances, and the fatigue piles up. I don’t feel like I’m failing, but I’m not performing like I used to, and that eats at me.

I can’t point to one thing that started this. Nothing major changed at work or at home—no death, no job loss, no fight with my wife. Just a slow slide into feeling hopeless, like I’m stuck in a fog that won’t lift. I don’t have thoughts of hurting myself or anything like that, but some days, I just wonder what the point is of pushing so hard when nothing feels satisfying anymore.
D020-D013_h010.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h010.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h011.question:
Lately, I just feel like everything’s piling up. I’ve been on edge all the time—jittery, can’t sit still, even small things make me jump. My hands shake sometimes when I’m drawing, and I keep checking my phone, worrying if I missed a message from my editor. Deadlines used to be stressful but manageable, but now I can’t seem to settle into a rhythm. I lie in bed at night, heart racing, replaying what I didn’t finish that day.  

I don’t know when it started, exactly—maybe a few weeks ago? It’s just… hard to care sometimes. I’ll stare at my screen for hours and can’t draw anything. I skip meals, forget to shower. I don’t hate my work, and it’s not like something huge happened—no breakup, no loss, nothing dramatic. But I feel off. Empty, kind of numb, but also wound too tight, like I’m both exhausted and buzzing.  

I keep thinking I’ll snap out of it, but it’s been hanging around. Not every day the same, but enough that I notice. I don’t want to let anyone down, but I’m not sure I can keep pretending I’m fine.
D020-D013_h011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D020-D013_h011.answer: C & A. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h012.question:
I’ve just been feeling… off for a few months now—maybe four? It started around the time my pharmacy shifted to this new overnight distribution system. I’m the lead pharmacist, so I’ve had to manage the errors, cover shifts when people bail, and absorb all the complaints from clinics about late meds. I can’t seem to relax, even at home. I keep replaying mistakes in my head, even small ones—like when I accidentally approved a refill that wasn’t authorized.  

Lately, I’ve been cutting out early, which isn’t like me. I’ll just drive instead of going back. Sometimes I end up at the highway interchange near the industrial park—just driving loops, windows down, music too loud. I don’t know why I do it. It’s not safe, but it feels like the only time my brain shuts off.  

I don’t know if it’s stress or something more. I’m sleeping more, but I wake up exhausted. I used to cook, go to spin class—now I just scroll. I’m not sure if I’m depressed or just burnt out. I’ve never had episodes like this before, but this job… it’s like I can’t catch up, no matter what I do.
D020-D013_h012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D020-D013_h012.answer: C & A. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I don’t know. It’s hard to track time when every day blurs together. I work with people at the end of their lives, so grief isn’t new to me, but lately, it’s like I’m carrying something heavier, even when I’m not at work. I don’t cry all the time or anything, but I’ll stand in the shower and realize I’ve been staring at the wall for twenty minutes, not feeling anything, just… empty. 

I used to enjoy walking my dog or meeting my sister for coffee, but now I cancel plans last minute. Not because I’m overwhelmed—more like I just don’t see the point. Sleep’s erratic—sometimes I can’t fall asleep until 3 a.m., other times I nap all afternoon. My appetite’s up and down; some days I forget to eat, others I finish a whole loaf of bread without noticing. 

I’m not sure if this started because of anything specific. My divorce was two years ago—was I expecting myself to be “over it” by now? I don’t feel sad about it exactly, but it still lives in the back of my mind. Nothing terrible’s happened at work—actually, things have been stable—but I don’t feel resilient anymore. I’m just… stuck. Not falling apart, not healing—just here.
D020-D013_h013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D020-D013_h013.answer: C & A. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h014.question:
I’ve just been feeling off for a while now—like, a few weeks, maybe a little over a month? It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started. I wake up and the thought of going to work at the café feels heavy, even though it’s not like I have a ton of responsibilities or anything intense. I try to push through, but some days I’m late because I just can’t get out of bed, or I end up calling out last minute. I don’t know, it feels like I’m just… going through the motions.

I’ve been really low, tearful for no reason, and sometimes I get weirdly angry over tiny things—like a customer complaining about the temperature of their oat milk latte. That’s not like me. I used to handle that stuff with a smile. Now I just feel brittle. I’ve lost interest in hanging out with friends, and I haven’t touched my sketchbook in weeks, which sucks because art used to be my thing.

I don’t know if it’s stress from moving out or the breakup or just adulting in general, but it doesn’t feel *catastrophic*—just… constant. Like a dull hum in the background that won’t shut off.
D020-D013_h014.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D020-D013_h014.answer: C & A. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h015.question:
I’ve just been feeling… off, lately. Like, things at work are piling up—the kitchen’s short-staffed, the hours are brutal, and my head’s always spinning. I snap at the guys on line when they’re not moving fast enough, which isn’t like me. My wife’s noticed it too—says I’ve been quiet at home, barely talking, just zoning out on the couch. I don’t feel like cooking for fun anymore, not even on days off. I used to love that. Now it all just feels heavy.  

I’m not really sleeping well—tossing and turning, waking up tired. Some days, I barely want to get out of bed, but I do, because I have to. I haven’t missed a shift. I don’t feel “cripplingly” sad or anything, but there’s this low hum of tension, like I’m dragging myself through everything. I’ve had a few drinks more than I should, just to unwind, but it’s not helping.  

It’s been like this for a couple of months, maybe? Nothing’s changed, but I keep waiting for it to lift and it just… doesn’t. I’m not sure if this is stress or something deeper. I just know I’m not myself.
D020-D013_h015.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D020-D013_h015.answer: C & A. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h016.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—hard to say exactly when it started. Life out on the rig is never easy; twelve-hour shifts, weeks away from home, sleeping in bunks like sardines. It’s always been rough, but lately, it just feels heavier. I’m more irritable, snap at guys over small things—stuff I’d normally shrug off. Some days I feel down for no clear reason, like a fog I can’t shake. I don’t enjoy the games we play during downtime like I used to, and I’ve skipped a few meals just because eating felt like another task.  

I’ve also started drinking more—beer on days off, sometimes enough to blackout. Not proud of it, but it numbs things for a bit. Once I even got into a shoving match with a coworker over a misplaced tool. That’s not me. I’ve never had trouble with conduct before.  

I don’t know if it’s the job, the isolation, or just turning thirty and feeling like I’m going nowhere. I’m not sure it’s “depression,” but I’m not myself. It’s not constant—some days are okay, even decent—but the bad ones keep piling up. I haven’t had thoughts of ending it or anything extreme, but I can’t say I haven’t felt empty enough to wonder what the point is.  

I thought I could tough it out, but now I’m wondering if I need help.
D020-D013_h016.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h016.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h017.question: I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I’ve lost track. Work’s been overwhelming lately; we’ve had staffing shortages, and I’m constantly picking up shifts or covering for others. I don’t know if it’s that, or just everything piling up, but I’ve been irritable, short-tempered—snapped at a customer last week, which isn’t like me. I felt terrible after. Some days I’m tearful for no clear reason, and other days I just feel hollow, like I’m going through the motions. I used to enjoy lunch with coworkers or picking up a new book, but now I don’t care. I go home, sit on the couch, and stare at the TV without really watching. I’m not sleeping well—either I can’t fall asleep or I wake up exhausted. I’ve skipped meals, forgotten appointments. A couple times, I’ve had a few too many glasses of wine to quiet my thoughts, which I never used to do. I can’t tell if this is just stress getting to me or something more. It’s not every moment of every day, but it’s always there, underneath everything. I’m managing work—barely—but I don’t feel like myself.
D020-D013_h017.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h017.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h018.question:
I’ve been feeling really down for a few months now—maybe four, maybe a bit more. Some days it’s just a heaviness, like I’m moving through water. I cry easily, even over small things—sometimes when I’m labeling an artist’s piece or hanging a show. It’s embarrassing. I used to find such satisfaction in the details, but now I just feel… empty. Hopeless? I don’t know if that’s too strong a word, but it lingers.  

I’m single, live alone, and my job has always been my anchor—curating, organizing, making meaning from art. But lately, I’m calling in sick more. I wake up late, skip breakfast, just sit. I don’t have the energy to call friends, and social things feel like work.  

There’ve been some changes—my mother moved into assisted living, and the gallery downsized—but I can’t say if that’s really *why* I feel this way. I don’t think I’m depressed-depressed, and it’s not like I’ve lost all interest. I still care, but it’s like everything’s muffled. I’m not sleeping terribly, and I haven’t had thoughts of not wanting to be here, but I’m just… off. I wanted to talk to you because it’s starting to affect my work—and I don’t want it to get worse.
D020-D013_h018.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h018.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h019.question:
I’ve been feeling really off since the comments started getting nasty online—what felt like months ago, though I can’t even tell anymore. At first, it was just this constant buzz in my chest, like I couldn’t sit still, couldn’t scroll without my hands shaking a little. I keep checking my phone, even in the middle of filming content, just in case someone’s saying something new. It’s exhausting.  

I don’t sleep well. Some nights I’m wide awake, replaying old posts, wondering if I sounded tone-deaf or fake. Other days, I can’t get out of bed. I cancel shoots, miss brand deadlines—stuff that used to matter so much just feels pointless now. I don’t know if it’s the stress or… something deeper.  

I used to love meeting followers in person, but now I dread being recognized. My heart races if my phone dings. It’s not like I’m sad all the time—I have moments where I laugh, where an idea excites me—but they don’t last. I just feel… fragile. Like I’m one post away from breaking.  

I don’t know when it started, or if it’s “bad enough” for help. It’s not like I’ve given up completely, but I’m not the person I was before the hate.
D020-D013_h019.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h019.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, I’ve lost track. It’s hard to explain. I wake up tired, even when I sleep enough, and some days, getting out of bed feels like climbing a mountain. I still care about my clients—matchmaking is my passion—but I find myself zoning out during calls, forgetting details I’d normally pick up right away. I used to love helping couples build their futures; now it sometimes feels like I’m just going through the motions.  

There’s this constant hum of worry, like I’m always waiting for something bad to happen, though nothing major has changed at work or at home. I get restless, fidgety—my husband says I’ve been snapping over little things. I don’t cry all the time, but I feel… fragile. Empty, maybe. I eat, I function, I show up—but I’m not really *there*.  

I keep thinking, “Is this just stress? Am I falling apart over nothing?” Nothing huge happened recently—no loss, no crisis—just the same life, somehow feeling heavier. I can’t tell if this is a phase or something more. I just want to feel like myself again.
D020-D013_h020.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D020-D013_h020.answer: C & D. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h021.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few weeks now—maybe a month? It’s hard to tell because the nights all blur together with my job. I work nights at the data center, mostly alone, just checking servers, making sure everything’s running. It’s quiet… too quiet sometimes. 

Lately, I’ve been down more than usual—just don’t care as much about things. I skip meals, or grab something quick, and I’ve stopped going out with friends. I used to game online after shifts, but now I just come home and crash. It’s not like I’m crying or anything, but there’s this numb heaviness, like I’m moving through fog.

I also feel on edge for no reason. My chest gets tight when I think about work, even though nothing’s changed. I had a buddy mention I look tired, which is normal for night shift, but I know it’s more than that. I haven’t been sleeping well during the day, and I’ll lie there, mind racing—about work, about nothing, about everything. 

I don’t know if it’s the isolation, or just how draining the job’s become, or maybe something personal I haven’t figured out yet. But it’s not bad enough to say “I need help,” but also not *not* a problem. I just… don’t feel like myself.
D020-D013_h021.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D020-D013_h021.answer: A & B. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h022.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to say. Since I retired two years ago, things just haven’t settled right. At first, I thought I’d enjoy the quiet, more time at home with my wife, but instead, I feel… on edge. I can’t sit still. My mind races, especially at night. I worry about things I never used to—my health, my daughter living across the country, whether I’m a burden. My hands sometimes tremble, and I catch myself breathing fast when nothing’s really happening. 

I don’t feel sad exactly, not like I imagine depression to be, but there’s a heaviness. I lost interest in the garden, used to be my pride. I still go through the motions—church on Sundays, coffee with old colleagues—but I feel detached, like I’m watching my life from the outside. I sleep, but not well. Appetite’s down a bit. I wake up tired. 

My wife says I’ve changed. I don’t snap, I’m not hopeless, but I’m not present either. Some days are better, but the anxiety sticks. It’s not like something terrible happened recently—it’s just… this slow drift. I wonder if I’m just adjusting poorly, or if this is how aging feels.
D020-D013_h022.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D020-D013_h022.answer: A & B. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h023.question: I’ve just been feeling… off, lately. It started a few months ago, maybe around the time my daughter moved across the country. I tell myself I should’ve expected it—she’s starting a new life, and that’s good, really it is—but since then, it’s like a fog settled in. I don’t cry every day, but sometimes I wake up with this heaviness, like I’m already behind. I used to enjoy knocking on doors, meeting people on my census route—there was a rhythm to it—but now I dread leaving the house. I still go, but I’m slow, distracted. My husband says I’ve been quiet, jumpy at noises. I’m not sure if I’m sad or just worried all the time. My mind races: Did I miss a section? Did I offend someone? Is something else going to change? I sleep, but not well. Wake up early, heart pounding. I don’t feel like myself, but I can’t say it’s one thing. It’s not like I can point to a single moment and say, “That’s when it broke.” It’s more like everything just… seeped in.
D020-D013_h023.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D020-D013_h023.answer: A & B. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h024.question: I’ve been feeling really off for a few months now—maybe four or five? It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started. Some days I’m just so down, like I can’t get excited about anything, not even things I used to love, like planning photo shoots for work or going out with friends. I’ll lie in bed thinking about all the tasks piling up, and instead of getting started, I just feel heavy. Other days, my mind races—I’ll be in the middle of writing a campaign and suddenly get this tightness in my chest, like I’m falling behind or about to mess up, even when everything’s on track. I’ve been snapping at coworkers over little things, then feeling guilty after. Sleep’s been all over the place. Either I can’t fall asleep, or I wake up at 4 a.m. with my mind buzzing. I don’t know if it’s because of work—it’s been busy lately, sure—but I can’t tell if that’s the real reason or if I’d feel this way regardless. I’m not having thoughts about not wanting to live or anything like that, but I do wonder why it’s so hard to shake this feeling, like I’m stuck in a fog. I just want to feel like myself again.
D020-D013_h024.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D020-D013_h024.answer: A & B. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D020-D013_h025.question:
I’ve been having a rough time lately—can’t really put my finger on when it started, but it’s been several weeks now. I’m not sleeping much, and when I do, it’s restless. Little things set me off—a siren, my kid’s toys on the floor, even my wife asking what’s wrong. I know she means well, but I just snap. I went on a call last week and didn’t suit up right—ignored protocol. My captain pulled me aside, said I’ve been “off.” He’s not wrong. I don’t feel like myself.

I’ve been drinking more than I should, a few bottles after shift just to quiet my head. Once, I drove home not fully sober—stupid, I know. But I can’t seem to care like I used to. Not about the rules, not about impressing anyone. I still go to work. Still get dressed. But inside, it’s like I’m running on fumes. I don’t enjoy grilling with the guys anymore. Don’t laugh like I used to at home. There’s no big reason for it—all my crew’s alive, my family’s safe—I just feel… hollow. I can’t tell if I’m just burnt out or if something deeper’s wrong.
D020-D013_h025.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D020-D013_h025.answer: A & B. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder
